ENVIRONMENTAL AWARENESS 
Anti-Litter and Anti-Graffiti Fund 
This grant scheme helps community groups to carry out anti-litter and anti-graffiti awareness 
campaigns in their local area. It has a particular focus on voluntary initiatives, and on involving 
schools and young people in anti-litter and anti-graffiti activities. 
▪ 
Examples of the kinds of initiatives supported by the grant scheme can include: 
▪ 
Providing anti-littering campaign materials, like anti-litter posters and stickers 
▪ 
Organising poster design competitions 
▪ 
Arranging interactive talks or plays involving schools and young people in anti-litter activities 
▪ 
Encouraging responsible dog owners to clean up after their pet in public places. 
€28,550 in grant aid and programme costs was allocated under the Anti-Litter and Anti-Graffiti 
scheme for 2024. This included 4 community led murals in Graiguenamanagh, Mooncoin, The Butts 
and Stoneyford.

9 
 
 
Team Up to Clean Up-Together for Kilkenny 
The commencement of a Roadside Litter campaign as part of the “Team Up to Clean Up-Together 
for Kilkenny” brand will commence the week commencing the 25th November.  This is a targeted 
campaign to help eliminate roadside litter at source. 
Many of our local and regional roads are heavily littered and are far too dangerous to litter pick with 
its heavy traffic volumes, dangerous bends and the absence of a hard shoulder. Like many other 
roads around the County, roadside litter is accumulating.  
Anti-Dumping Initiative 2024 
As part of the Anti-Dumping Initiative, Kilkenny County Council funded the development of a 
mural in Francis McManus Square which has become a blackspot for rubbish and dumping in recent 
years. The project was co-led by Keep Kilkenny Beautiful and Ossory Youth and is demonstrative 
of what can be achieve by good will, teamwork and environmental stewardship. 
 
 
 
Savour Kilkenny Food Festival- Waste Baseline and Characterisation 
Savour Kilkenny has been working on sustainability measures for almost half of its 16 year history. 
Waste related plans for 2024 included eliminating disposable cups through 2gocup, provision of a 
refill water point, and demonstrating use of mygug composting.  
Through the Anti Dumping Initiative 2024, the Environmental Department procured consultants to 
undertake waste compositional analysis and an observational assessment of the Festival with a view 
to creating a report of recommendations identifying key waste prevention and management goals 
and policies for the development of the festival and an overall strategy with an incremental approach 
across many actions.  
Kilkenny Groups Excel at Tidy Towns Awards 2024 
The remarkable commitment and efforts of community organizations in Kilkenny have been 
celebrated at this year's Tidy Towns awards. These annual accolades honour communities dedicated 
to enhancing their local surroundings, showcasing the remarkable contributions of various groups 
throughout the County. 
Inistioge Tidy Towns was honoured with both a Gold Medal and 1st Place in the County Awards 
category, while Coan Tidy Towns secured the Endeavour Award for the biggest improvement by 
an entrant in each County from the previous year. 
Keep Kilkenny Beautiful continued its success by retaining its Gold Medal and finishing in 2nd place 
in the County Awards. 
Tullahought Tidy Towns was awarded “Highly Commended” for their work under the National 
Pollinator Programme during the ceremony held at Croagh Park on November 1st, 2024. Their 
unwavering dedication to cleanliness, improving green spaces, and promoting community pride 
has distinguished them in this competitive field. 
This year Kilkenny had two new entrants under the National Competition with Graiguenamanagh, 
and Owning demonstrating their exceptional efforts and work for their respective communities. All 
of whom scored strongly for their first time around.

Green Teams National Programme 2024 
Green Teams in public sector organisations are essential for driving sustainability initiatives, 
reducing resource consumption, and fostering a culture of environmental responsibility across the 
workplace.  
Over 60 organisations have already participated in the Green Teams National Programme, designed 
to empower workplace environmental champions and green team members in Ireland. It includes 
three interactive online sessions covering sustainability, resource efficiency, green team 
management, and staff engagement. 
Led by the EAO in conjunction with the Climate Action Team, 8 staff members of Kilkenny County 
Council are participating in this EPA developed programme for Q4 of 2024.  
This EPA Green Enterprise scheme, equips participants with the practical knowledge and tools to 
make sustainable practices happen on the ground. Participants will gain technical skills, access peer 
support, and receive resources to enhance their green initiatives. GTNP-Online-Programme-
Summary_2022.pdf.aspx (caro.ie)

Bring Banks Usage 
The Council provides and manages 47 Bring Centers across the City and County.  A total of 1703 
tonnes of recyclables were collected from our Bring Centers to date in 2024.  This represents a 1% 
decrease from the same period in 2023. Aldi - Kilkenny City (15 tonnes collected),  Loughboy 
shopping centre (11 tonnes collected) Lidl - Johnswell, Kilkenny City (10 tonnes collected) and are 
the busiest locations in the City. Aldi - Ferrybank (11 tonnes collected), Lidl - Thomastown (7 tonnes 
collected) and Graiguemanagh (6 tonnes collected) are the busiest outside of the City.  Environment 
staff are continuing to work very closely with our service providers to ensure the collection service 
is in keeping with demand, especially around long weekends and holiday periods.  
Dunmore Civic Amenity Site (CAS) 
The annual Bulk Waste week at Dunmore ran for the first week of October 2024. This is an Ant-
Dumping Initiative (ADI) which sets out to encourage the public to clean up their unwanted bulk 
waste and furniture in the correct manner at an authorised facility. Domestic loads of any size could 
be disposed of at Dunmore for a set fee of €5 for the duration of the Bulk Waste week. This resulted 
in almost 12 tonnes of bulky fabric covered furniture and almost 38 tonnes of timer deposited at the 
site. The month of October also saw 114 tonnes of Municipal Solid Waste, 86 tonnes of Municipal 
Dry Waste and 33 tonnes of green garden waste.

Water Quality – Farm Inspections 
Farm inspections are still ongoing and are on track to reach 241 inspections by the end of the year. 
Septic tank Inspections 
The Environment office has completed 61 inspections which is 10 more than the target of 51.  We 
will be also closing out the remaining historical open advisory notices dating back to 2013 and this 
process is already in motion with people contacting us hoping to have them closed out after contact 
was made with letters.  Septic tank grant approvals are currently ongoing. Upgrade works and work 
approvals are being carried out with various applicants who are applying for the grant.  The 
Environment Office are still dealing with a large volume of queries in relation to the criteria for  
eligibility for the grant. 
Section 4 Discharge Licences 
The Environment office will be closing out all 25 section 4 discharge licenses in Q4. 
Misconnections 
The Council is currently in the process of investigating a serious misconnection in Thomastown. 
Investigation has been completed through review of cameras at local businesses. Review identified 
a truck pouring waste water into a manhole which is discharging into a river. The license plate of 
the truck has not yet been identified and more investigation will be required. Samples were taken 
and tested from the river showing very poor results. 
Environment Complaints 
All Environmental complaints received are logged on the CRM (Customer Relations Management) 
System.  The number of complaints that have been received and logged for October 2024 is 85 
compared to 82 for the same period last year.  The number of complaints received in the ten months 
to the end of October 2024 is up 8% when compared to the same ten-month period in 2023. The 
nature of these complaints included littering, illegal dumping, burning of waste and abandoned 
cars.  The majority continue to be related to littering and illegal dumping.  Whilst every effort is 
made to bring unacceptable environmental practice into compliance, Environment Enforcement 
staff continue to manage significant enforcement cases progressing through prosecution cases. 
Noise 
Kilkenny County Council with support of Noise Consultants Limited have completed the draft 
Noise Action Plan 2024-2028. The draft Noise Action Plan is aimed at strategic long-term 
management of environmental noise from major roads. It does not apply to noise from domestic 
activities, neighbourhood noise, noise at workplaces or noise inside means of transport or due to 
military activities in military areas.  
The plan is now at the public consultation stage between 30th October and 11th of November 2024 
with submissions being accepted until 25th November 2024. The final plan is on target to be 
submitted to the EPA in December 2024. 
 
During the month of November 2 submissions have been received. These will be reviewed and 
closed out appropriately following discussions with the noise consultant

Woodstock to South East Greenway Link

Tree Maintenance Programme 
Each year, our office receives numerous inquiries from both Elected Members and the public 
regarding tree maintenance. This prompts an assessment of each tree's health and condition to 
determine the necessary maintenance, if any. The dormant period of trees is the optimal time for 
such work.  Currently, we are committed to tree maintenance in Inistoige, Cuffsgrange, Paulstown, 
Ballyragget, Kilkenny City, and Thomastown. Our tree maintenance programme commenced in 
earnest at the beginning of November.  The works are divided into geographical lots and the 
tendering process to engage the services of specialist tree surgeons is ongoing.  
Woodstock Gardens & Arboretum   
Autumn has marked the commencement of our key 
seasonal tasks. The wildflower meadow has been cut 
and gathered. Extensive pruning and mulching has 
been carried out in the playground area, including 
pruning of the willow tunnel and crown lifting of trees 
to allow more light into the playground. The woodland 
arboretum is also receiving a tidy-up around the base 
of the trees. 
Planned renovation works will take place in the walled 
garden over the winter months, rejuvenating the fruit 
bushes and espalier fruit trees. Additionally, extensive 
weeding and mulching of the herbaceous border will 
ensure it looks its best for the coming year. 
Season tickets for the 2025 season, costing just €50 for 
12 months access, will be promoted as ideal Christmas 
gifts over the coming weeks.

Works are continuing to secure the rear elevation of the house, fronting onto the Winter Garden, 
which entails the stabilisation of the window opes with steel frames and tie bars, as required. This

removed. These works are in addition to the clearance of sapling trees and extensive vegetation to 
the rear of the house carried out earlier in the year.

consecutive years. However, in the case of joint tenancies only one tenant is now required to

The existence of a professional Fire & Rescue Service is fundamental to public and personal safety.

emergencies that occur 24 hours per day/7 days per week/365 days per year.  The Brigades have

Retained Firefighters are men and women who are on call to respond to a range of emergencies.

Training 
Kilkenny County Council’s Fire & Rescue Service are obliged under the Fire Services Acts 1981 and 
2003 and the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work Act 2005 to ensure that our Firefighters and Officers 
are adequately trained and competent to deal with tasks and varying roles they may encounter in 
the performance of their duties. 
All personnel responding to Fire & Rescue Service incidents require a minimum level of training to 
meet core requirements.  In addition, many personnel also require further training for specialist or 
supervisory roles.  Furthermore, a number of Fire and Rescue Service personnel have completed 
Instructor Courses in order that they in turn can instruct and direct delivery of training 
sessions/courses.  Personnel also require appropriate refresher training in all of the above

Kilkenny Swift Project 
Swifts are a migratory bird and spend their summers in 
Ireland.  Preferring to nest in cracks and cervices 
unfortunately their numbers are in decline due to the loss 
of nesting sites.    Three sets of swift nest boxes were 
installed under the supervision of BirdWatch Ireland at the 
Councils Thomastown Area Office in October thanks to the 
support of area engineer Declan Murphy.  A caller system 
was also installed to encourage the swifts to investigate 
these potential nesting sites when they return to Ireland 
next May.   
This project was a recommendation out of the County Swift Survey and the installation was funded 
by the National Parks and Wildlife Service under the Local Biodiversity Action Fund.  Various 
council properties across the County have been examined for their suitability and the plan is to have 
more installations in the future. The Biodiversity Officer is also collaborating with other agencies to 
identify suitable sites to encourage swift box installation as a positive biodiversity action. 
Southeast Nightjar Project 
BirdWatch Ireland promoted the results of the Nightjar Survey which took place over the summer 
in Wexford and Kilkenny.  The mysterious and elusive Nightjar is a summer visitor, it can be 
incredibly difficult to spot, only revealing its presence after dark, when the male engages in it’s 
hypnotic ‘churring’ song. 
Nightjars were once more common and widespread in Ireland.   
However, the numbers completing the journey to Ireland from 
African 
wintering 
grounds 
each 
May 
have 
diminished 
dramatically. This is thought to be related to habitat loss and a 
decrease in large insects due to the use of pesticides.  
The aim of the survey was to confirm whether Nightjar still remain 
in Ireland and to learn more about this enigmatic species to help 
inform its conservation. The Nightjar survey concentrated on 
some of the most suitable remaining areas for Nightjar in counties 
Kilkenny and Wexford.  
The survey revealed two sites with nightjar’s present.  Subsequent monitoring of these sites 
provided confirmation that one of these pairs bred successfully.  The survey was completed by 
BirdWatch Ireland, supported and promoted by the Biodiversity Officer and funded by the Local 
Biodiversity Action Fund from the National Parks and Wildlife Service.
